text.p: Mount Edon Gold Mines (Australia) Ltd said on Wednesday a A$2.15 per share joint takeover offer earlier unveiled by Camelot Resources NL and Canada's Teck Corp was "opportunistic" and advised shareholders to take no immediate action.
Mount Edon share price has traded up to A$3.50 a share in the last 12 months without a premium for control, Mount Edon wsaid in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
"This offer is unsolicited and is considered opportunistic," Mount Edon said
Mount Edon's board will meet shortly to consider the offer and appoint professional advisers, the company said.
Camelot said earlier on Wednesday the offer for the Australian gold producer would be made through a jointly owned special purpose company with Teck called Reachwest Pty Ltd.
Mt Edon shares jumped 64 cents to close at A$2.09 on turnover of 12.6 million shares on Wednesday, while Camelot stock was steady at 30 cents on turnover of 1.1 million shares.
The Camelot-Teck offer values Mount Edon at A$158 million.
